_about: ASSUMPTIONS, not measurements. Every business figure in outputs/impact_estimate.json is computed from these values and from rates measured on the synthetic data. Change a value, re-run `python scripts/run_phase6.py`, and the estimate and its sensitivity table update. Currency is INR only because the project's records are Indian; all amounts are placeholders to be replaced with the organisation's own.

customer_base_records.note: Size of the customer file the rates are scaled to. Rates are measured per record on the synthetic data.

messages_per_record_per_year.note: Marketing and service messages (email/SMS) one record receives per year.

share_of_messages_reaching_duplicates.note: Share of campaigns that do not already de-duplicate on the sending side, so a duplicate record really is messaged twice.

cost_per_message_inr.note: Blended cost of one email/SMS including platform fees. Does not include customer annoyance or unsubscribe cost.

cost_per_wrong_merge_inr.note: Cost of one cluster that mixes two customers: a misdirected message, a support call, a manual split.

records_affected_per_over_merged_cluster.note: Records whose communication is wrong while a cluster mixes customers.

reviewer_minutes_per_pair.note: Time for an analyst to judge one pair from the evidence columns of the review queue.

review_checkpoint_pairs_per_1000_records.note: How much of the ranked queue is reviewed. 50 per 1,000 records is about 250 pairs on the 5,171-record dev data, a point on the simulated curve in outputs/review_simulation.csv.

reviewer_accuracy.note: Chance a reviewer's verdict is right. Only 1.0 and 0.95 are simulated in outputs/review_simulation.csv, so those are the two allowed values. This selects which simulated curve supplies the review rates; it is not varied in the sensitivity table.

relative_change.note: Each assumption above is moved down and up by this fraction, one at a time, to show which ones the estimate depends on.
